content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text adjudicates cited verses and their answered status for a link, so K-G4 governs whether any verse may be counted as an unanswered witness.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"'counts as an unanswered witness' and 'If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it': one reading treats any mention of a verse's force as counting it; the other, which I adopt, limits the rule to verses counted toward a broken link as unanswered, so an UNDERDETERMINED ruling that says 'answered' does not count them.","why":"The judge does not count any cited verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; it calls the dispute UNDERDETERMINED and says the cited material was answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5."}
